title: Segura v. Sandiganbayan
summary: The Supreme Court distinguished between evident bad faith and gross negligence under Section 3(e) of RA 3019. A conviction for violation of the Anti-Graft Law requires proof that the public officer acted with manifest partiality, evident bad faith, or gross inexcusable negligence.
doctrine: Section 3(e) of RA 3019 may be committed either by dolo (with evident bad faith or manifest partiality) or by culpa (through gross inexcusable negligence). The two modes are distinct and separate from each other. Evidence of evident bad faith requires proof of a palpably fraudulent and dishonest purpose.
fullText:
CARPIO, J.:

The issue is whether the petitioner is guilty of violating Section 3(e) of Republic Act No. 3019, the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act.

Section 3(e) of RA 3019 punishes a public officer who causes any undue injury to any party or gives any private party any unwarranted benefits through manifest partiality, evident bad faith, or gross inexcusable negligence.

Evident bad faith connotes a palpably and patently fraudulent and dishonest purpose to do moral obliquity or conscious wrongdoing. It is different from gross inexcusable negligence which involves want of even slight care, acting or omitting to act in a situation where there is a duty to act.
